scope: Proposition 6.6 of the manuscript “Scale and conformal symmetry in four-dimensional operational quantum field theory” (preprints/Scale-and-conformal-symmetry-in-four-dimensional-operational-quantum-field-theory-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 282 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 485a44682f95ef0d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 70. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let a be a physical field or S, and let f have support in a small real source patch. Given a double-cone neighborhood of its support, there are bounded operations AR(f) in that neighborhood, for dyadic R → ∞, such that for one fixed exponent q ∥AR(f)∥ ≤ CRq , (6.10) ∥AR(f)Ω − a(f)∥ + ∥AR(f)∗ Ω − a† ( ¯ f)∥ ≤ CN R−N (N = 1, 2, . . .). (6.11) For each prescribed N, constants are uniform on balls of finitely many test seminorms. When patches and localization margins shrink to size ε in a fixed compact set, these constants cost at most fixed inverse powers of ε. The approximants need not depend linearly on f.
